chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) said:
Water is the chief of drinks in this world and the Hereafter.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Isa ibn Abdillah, by his chain — similar to it.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَة: This world and the Hereafter — emphasizing the eternal and universal validity of this ruling
key_terms.الشَّرَاب: Drink/Beverage — refers to all liquid consumables; water is declared their master
key_terms.سَيِّد: Chief/Master — the highest-ranking one in a category, used here to signify water's supreme status among beverages

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the status of water among drinks?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) proclaimed that water holds the highest rank among all drinks in both this world and the Hereafter. The hadith is then confirmed by a second, shorter chain that corroborates the same narration. This teaching, in the context of early Islamic jurisprudence on food and drink, elevated water above all other beverages, establishing its primacy as a fundamental blessing from God. The audience of early Shia scholars would have understood this as both a dietary guideline and a spiritual reminder of water's divine significance.
